title: The admirable friend
hook: Ananda says good friendship is half the holy life; the Buddha says it is the whole (SN 45.2)

segments.voice: Yesterday: finding a sangha, and your line, you need people. Did you look up one place near you where people practice together? Day three hundred twenty.

Ananda, the Buddha's cousin, spent about twenty-five years at his side as his attendant. He carried the bowl, remembered the talks, and knew better than anyone what the teacher's days were like. One day he came to the Buddha with a thought he was clearly pleased with. He had worked out how much of the spiritual life depends on good friends, and he was being generous: he said half. The Buddha's answer is one of the most quoted lines in the whole canon. Today: the admirable friend.
screen: `ANANDA, TWENTY-FIVE YEARS AT HIS SIDE.` → `A GENEROUS THOUGHT.` → `HE SAID HALF.`

segments.voice: The scene is in a short discourse in the Samyutta Nikaya. Ananda says, in paraphrase: good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship, this is half of the holy life. And the Buddha answers: not so, Ananda. It is the whole of the holy life. Someone with admirable friends, he says, can be expected to walk the whole noble eightfold path. Then he points to himself. It's by relying on him as an admirable friend, he says, that beings are freed from birth, aging and death. The Pali is kalyanamitta. Kalyana means good, beautiful, lovely. Mitta means friend, from the same family as metta, loving-kindness, the first word of this path. So an admirable friend isn't just a pleasant one. It's someone whose goodness rubs off on you. The Buddha says elsewhere that when the mind isn't yet ripe, the very first thing that helps it ripen is an admirable friend. And in a long talk to a young householder, he describes the real friend: one who helps you when you're careless, who's the same in good times and bad, who points you toward what's good, and who is glad when you do well. Notice what that means for you. Friendship isn't a nice extra beside the practice, something for weekends. It's the practice's ground. Who you spend time with shapes what you think, what you laugh at, what you let slide. And it runs both ways: you can be that friend for someone. The whole of the path.
screen: `HALF? NOT SO, ANANDA.` · `KALYANA, GOOD. MITTA, FRIEND.` · `THE FIRST THING THAT RIPENS THE MIND.` · `THE REAL FRIEND, DESCRIBED.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE OF THE PATH.`

segments.voice: For this sit, name one admirable friend. Someone whose goodness has rubbed off on you, alive or not, near or far. Picture their face. Remember one moment when they pointed you toward something good. Silently thank them. Then turn it around: think of one person for whom you might be that friend. Let them both rest in your mind, and then rest in the breath. The bell holds the time.
Kalyanamitta. The admirable friend, whose goodness rubs off on you. Not half the holy life, the Buddha says: the whole of it.
Your line: the whole of the path. Today, send one short message to the friend you named, and tell them one thing they gave you. Day three hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Buddhists across traditions treat the admirable friend, a teacher or a fellow practitioner, as central to practice, and many describe choosing good companions as part of the path itself.

match.prompt: match the pieces of the admirable friend.

myth: the Buddha agreed that friendship is half of the holy life
he said: not so, Ananda. it is the whole of the holy life.
mitta, friend, is related to metta, loving-kindness
the Buddha called himself an admirable friend
he said relying on him as an admirable friend frees beings from birth, aging and death.

fork.setup: you're Ananda. you've just told the Buddha that good friendship is half of the holy life. what does he say?
options: not so: it's the whole of the holy life.
fork.reveal: not so, Ananda. it is the whole of the holy life. someone with admirable friends can be expected to walk the whole eightfold path.

trapdoor: what you thought: a good friend is a nice extra.
what it means: the Buddha calls admirable friendship the whole of the holy life.
what a scholar hears: in SN 45.2 the Buddha names himself the kalyāṇamitta; in the Meghiya Sutta (AN 9.1) admirable friendship is the first condition for the mind's ripening.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2, Upaddha Sutta (half the holy life)
Anguttara Nikaya 9.1 / Udana 4.1, Meghiya (the first condition)
Digha Nikaya 31, Sigalovada Sutta (the true friend)

notes: SN 45.2 paraphrased (no public-domain translation quoted). Rhys Davids' DN 31 (Dialogues III, 1921) is public domain in the US but not quoted.
Ananda as attendant for about 25 years: traditional figure; confirm.
The four kinds of true friend in DN 31 are summarized loosely: confirm.
